verses.1: This is what the LORD says about Moab: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn back. Because they burned the bones of the king of Edom into dust.
verses.2: I will send fire into Moab, and it will devour the foundations of the city walls. Moab will die in distress, with a cry and with the sound of a trumpet.
verses.3: I will destroy their judge from among them, and kill all their officials with him, says the LORD.
verses.4: This is what the LORD says about Judah: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn back. Because they despised the teaching of the LORD and did not keep his statutes, and were led astray by the worthless things their ancestors followed after.
verses.5: I will send fire into Judah, and it will devour the foundations of Jerusalem.
verses.6: This is what the LORD says about Israel: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn back. Because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of sandals.
verses.7: Those who trample the dust of the earth on the heads of the poor and push aside the path of the humble, and a man and his father go to the same girl, in order to profane my holy name.
verses.8: And they draped garments in the form of shrouds over every altar, and drank wine from the bowls of guilt in the house of their God.
verses.9: Yet I brought down the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of a cedar, and who was strong as an oak. I destroyed its fruit above, and its roots below.
verses.10: And I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you through the wilderness forty years, to inherit the land of the Amorite.
verses.11: And I raised up prophets from among your children, and nazirites from your young. Is there no such thing among the people of Israel? says the LORD.
verses.12: But you gave the nazirites wine to drink, and commanded the prophets, saying, "Do not prophesy."
verses.13: Therefore, behold, I will roll under you as a cart full of sheaves rolls.
verses.14: And escape will perish from the swift, and the strong will not retain his might, and the warrior will not save his life.
verses.15: The archer will not stand, and the swift of foot will not escape, nor the rider on the horse save his life.
verses.16: The brave will find no courage in the mighty, but the naked will flee that day, says the LORD.

notes:
Notes
- v. 7: "the same girl" refers to the Hebrew "הַנַּעֲרָה" (ha-na'arah), which is rendered as "girl" to maintain clarity and context.
- v. 8: "in the form of shrouds" is a contextual interpretation of "חֲבֻלִים" (khavulim), which literally means "tied" or "bound," but the metaphor here seems to be of garments tied as a burial shroud.
- v. 13: "as a cart full of sheaves rolls" reflects the Hebrew metaphor for unstoppable destruction, maintaining the image without archaic phrasing.

[1] This is what the LORD says about Moab: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn back. Because they burned the bones of the king of Edom into dust.

[2] I will send fire into Moab, and it will devour the foundations of the city walls. Moab will die in distress, with a cry and with the sound of a trumpet.

[3] I will destroy their judge from among them, and kill all their officials with him, says the LORD.

[4] This is what the LORD says about Judah: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn back. Because they despised the teaching of the LORD and did not keep his statutes, and were led astray by the worthless things their ancestors followed after.

[5] I will send fire into Judah, and it will devour the foundations of Jerusalem.

[6] This is what the LORD says about Israel: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn back. Because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of sandals.

[7] Those who trample the dust of the earth on the heads of the poor and push aside the path of the humble, and a man and his father go to the same girl, in order to profane my holy name.

[8] And they draped garments in the form of shrouds over every altar, and drank wine from the bowls of guilt in the house of their God.

[9] Yet I brought down the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of a cedar, and who was strong as an oak. I destroyed its fruit above, and its roots below.

[10] And I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you through the wilderness forty years, to inherit the land of the Amorite.

[11] And I raised up prophets from among your children, and nazirites from your young. Is there no such thing among the people of Israel? says the LORD.

[12] But you gave the nazirites wine to drink, and commanded the prophets, saying, "Do not prophesy."

[13] Therefore, behold, I will roll under you as a cart full of sheaves rolls.

[14] And escape will perish from the swift, and the strong will not retain his might, and the warrior will not save his life.

[15] The archer will not stand, and the swift of foot will not escape, nor the rider on the horse save his life.

[16] The brave will find no courage in the mighty, but the naked will flee that day, says the LORD.

Notes
- v. 7: "the same girl" refers to the Hebrew "הַנַּעֲרָה" (ha-na'arah), which is rendered as "girl" to maintain clarity and context.
- v. 8: "in the form of shrouds" is a contextual interpretation of "חֲבֻלִים" (khavulim), which literally means "tied" or "bound," but the metaphor here seems to be of garments tied as a burial shroud.
